key_insight: Elenchos shows that LLMs can often detect that a formal system changed, but they frequently fail to infer the exact latent rule mutations causing the behavior change.
engineering_relevance: For AI system design and debugging, this suggests current LLMs are better at spotting anomalies than explaining root causes, so human-in-the-loop verification remains important for mutation diagnosis.
method: Introduce Elenchos, a generative evaluation framework for abductive reasoning.
Pose mutation detection and attribution as an inverse problem over formal systems like the lambda-calculus.
Test frontier and mid-tier LLMs on whether they can identify if a mutation occurred and recover the underlying rule changes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a consistent detection-attribution dissociation, with performance dropping notably under interacting mutations and only modest gains from larger reasoning budgets.
watch_item: Results are based on a formal-system benchmark, so generalization to open-world scientific or engineering settings may be limited.
paper_title: LLMs Can See the Smoke but not the Fire: Evaluating Abductive Reasoning with Elenchos
